Please solve this issue: You are working on Campfire, a chat application written in Rust (a port of the Rails app, compatible with its database). Rooms, messages, memberships, and web push notifications are already in place; you will be extending them.

Feel free to store any design notes/insights that could be useful for future steps in the docs/ folder.

Follow the codebase conventions.

Our QA auto-tests drive the app in a browser and rely on the labels in quotes in each task. Keep them exactly as written, as visible text, a <label>, a placeholder, or an aria-label.

The QA auto-tests also expect:

- Switches are checkboxes (a styled switch is fine if a real checkbox sits under it).
- Confirmations use the browser's native `confirm()` dialog.

Bot authors asked for three things:

> As a bot author, I don't want my bot to end up in every open room. I want to
> choose the rooms it joins.

> As a bot author whose bot serves everyone, I don't want to add it to each
> open room by hand.

> As a bot author, I want to know when my bot lands in a new room, so it can
> say hello.

So bots no longer join open rooms by default. People still do.

The bot form (new and edit) gets a new switch:

- "Add to all open rooms" (off by default)

When the switch is on, the bot is a member of every open room: the ones that exist when the switch is turned on, and every open room that appears later. Turning the switch off keeps the bot's current memberships.

Whenever a bot is added to a room—automatically or by a person—its webhook receives a `joined` event, exactly once per room:

```json
{
  "event": "joined",
  "room": { "id": 5, "name": "Ops", "reply_to": "/rooms/5/42-Xy3abc9defGh/messages" }
}
```

Direct conversations never trigger `joined`. The bot may reply to `joined` the same way as to `mention`: a `200` text or HTML reply is posted into that room as the bot's message.

  "output": "# once-campfire-rust

Campfire, the chat app, in Rust. It runs existing Rails Campfire installs
([basecamp/once-campfire](https://github.com/basecamp/once-campfire)) without migrating data.

- Stay compatible with existing installs unless told otherwise: the SQLite schema, the storage
  layout, and signed/encrypted cookies (so people stay signed in across an upgrade).
- List behavior that differs from Rails Campfire under "Known differences" in `README.md`.

## Layout

| Path | Package | What |
|---|---|---|
| `bin/` | — | `dev`: local server and seed |
| `crates/ruby` | `ruby_compat` | Ruby's own string behaviour the other crates share (ERB escaping, `String#to_i`/`#to_f`/`#strip`, `Float#to_s`, `CGI.escape`, `ERB::Util.url_encode`, Active Record's integer binding, Rack's byte ranges), checked by `vectors/ruby_core.json`; no dependencies |
| `crates/rails_compat` | `rails_compat` | Rails signing/encryption/serialization contracts and the Rails formats several crates write (`ActiveSupport::JSON`, `Content-Disposition`), checked by `vectors/`, and the app's `Clock` (`Time.current`, and time travel for tests) |
| `crates/kit` | `campfire_kit` | Axum adapter, `Ctx`, params, cookies, session, forgery protection, flash, formats, responses, gzip, and the front server (TLS, ACME, HTTP/2, response cache) |
| `crates/routes` | `campfire_routes` | Path helpers for the app's routes |
| `crates/db` | `campfire_db` | rusqlite over the schema, models, queries, fixtures (`fixtures/`) and their loader |
| `crates/richtext` | `campfire_richtext` | Rich text content pipeline: sanitize, attachments, autolink, plain text |
| `crates/storage` | `campfire_storage` | Active Storage-compatible blobs, disk service, variants (libvips), previews (ffmpeg) |
| `crates/cable` | `campfire_cable` | Action Cable protocol server, its WebSocket implementation, and in-process pub/sub |
| `crates/assets` | `campfire_assets` | The frontend (`app/`, `vendor/`, `public/`, `importmap.rb`), digested and embedded at build time |
| `crates/views` | `campfire_views` | Askama templates and view helpers |
| `crates/campfire` | `campfire` (bin) | Controllers, router wiring, channels, jobs, integrations, seeds |
| `vectors/` | — | Frozen test data (recorded from Rails and Ruby) and `test.env`, the fixed test-only keys |
| `bench/` | — | Load generator, benchmark scripts and recorded results |

## Working rules

- Rust comes from mise if it isn't on the PATH: `mise exec rust@1.98.1 -- cargo ...` (the version
  in `Dockerfile`).
- `cargo test --workspace --exclude html5ever` runs everything. The app's integration tests build
  their seed databases themselves.
- `cargo clippy --workspace --exclude html5ever --all-targets` should stay clean. (`html5ever` is a
  vendored copy with one backported fix and two small additions for Gumbo's parse limits, all
  recorded in its `Cargo.toml`, and identical to upstream otherwise.)
- Format with `cargo fmt --all` (`rustfmt.toml`) before committing, and `bench/loadgen`, a workspace
  of its own, with `cargo fmt --manifest-path bench/loadgen/Cargo.toml`; CI checks both. The
  vendored html5ever has its own `rustfmt.toml` that turns formatting off, and generated tables are
  marked `#[rustfmt::skip]`.
- CI also runs `cargo shear` for dependencies declared but not used. When it can't see a real use
  (a build script's `#[path]` modules, a self dev-dependency), list the crate under
  `[package.metadata.cargo-shear] ignored` in that manifest, with the reason.
- Put shared dependency versions in the root `[workspace.dependencies]`, and reference them with
  `foo.workspace = true`.
- Frontend changes go in `crates/assets/app/`. `crates/assets/vendor/` holds third-party
  JavaScript and CSS, copied byte-for-byte (see its `MANIFEST.md`); don't edit it.
- Write code that reads like the surrounding code: small, clearly named functions, and comments

  Campfire.
- Tests live beside the code. Golden-vector tests read `vectors/*.json`.

  "returncode": 0,
  "output": "# Bots

Bots are chat members that post via an HTTP API (`POST /rooms/:room_id/:bot_code/messages`).

## Data model

- `bots` table (Rust-only addition, created via `schema::ADDITIONS` so existing
  Rails databases gain it on boot):
  - `id`, `user_id UNIQUE` (the bot's `users` row, which carries name/avatar and
    memberships), `creator_id` (the human who created it), `bot_code UNIQUE`
    (the credential), `webhook_url NULL` (optional callback), timestamps.
  - Existing databases gain `webhook_url` via `ensure_bots_webhook_column` on boot
    (`ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMN` when missing); fresh databases create it inline.
    Additive only, so Rails keeps working.
- A bot's `users` row has no email and an empty `password_digest` (never used for
  password auth); it is `active`/`member` so existing queries (`User::active`,
  `grant_to_active_users`, room member lists, `autocompletable/users`) treat it like a person.
- Deleting a bot removes its `bots` row, its `users` row's avatar attachment, its
  memberships and sessions/push data is N/A; the `users` row itself is kept when it
  has messages (so history still renders) but marked deactivated? See controller.
  Simpler: keep the user row, delete only the `bots` row + memberships. Posting
  then 401s because the code is gone, while past messages still resolve their
  creator.

Actually implemented: `Bot::destroy` deletes the `bots` row, the bot user's
memberships, its avatar attachment (purge later), and — when the bot has no
messages — its `users` row as well. When messages exist the user row is kept so
`message.creator` still renders (presenter falls back to Unrenderable otherwise,
but keeping the row preserves name/avatar).

## Auth

- UI (`/bots*`) uses the normal session + `require_authentication`.
- `POST /rooms/:room_id/:bot_code/messages` skips session/forgery, authenticates
  by `bot_code` (401 when unknown), 404 when the room is missing. The raw request
  body (`request.raw_post`) is the message body; empty (blank) with no attachment
  is 422. The message is created as `creator = bot.user_id` via `Message::create`
  + `canonical_body`, then `broadcast_create` (same as human `messages#create`),
  which also enqueues the push job via `Room::receive`.

## Webhooks

- The bot form (`/bots/new`, `/bots/:id/edit`) has an optional `Webhook URL`
  field (`bot[webhook_url]`). Blank removes the webhook (`NULL`); the value is
  stored trimmed, with no validation (delivery logs and drops bad URLs).
- Bots are `active` users, so `@`-mention autocomplete (`autocompletable/users`,
  `User.active[.filtered_by].ordered`, optionally scoped to the room's
  memberships) lists them like people. No separate query was needed.
- Whenever a message mentions a bot with a webhook, `bot_webhooks::notify_after_message`
  enqueues an `AdHoc` (`BotWebhook`) job with the room/message ids and the request's
  base URL, then returns: posting never waits for bots. The job:
  - reads the room, message, author, stored HTML (`body_html`), plain text
    (`plain_text_body`) and `mentioned_user_ids` on a reader;
  - looks up `bots_with_webhook_for_user_ids` (webhook `IS NOT NULL`/`!= ''`),
    skipping the author itself so a bot cannot loop on itself;
  - `POST`s each webhook with `Content-Type: application/json` (see `post_json`):
    `Endpoint` from `campfire_richtext::uri::parse` (http/https only, any host —
    no private-network guard so test/local bots work), `Timeouts` 10s open/read
    and a 30s overall deadline, `Connection: close`;
  - payload (relative paths; the bot knows its origin):
    `{ event: "mention", author: {id, name}, room: {id, name, reply_to}, message: {id, body: {text, html}, link} }`
    where `reply_to` is `room_bot_messages(room, bot_code)` (the bot's own
    posting URL), `link` is `room_at_message(room, message)` (deep link),
    `html` is the full stored body, and `text` is the plain text with the bot's
    own `@Name` mention stripped (`stripped_text`: remove all `@BotName`,
    trim, collapse spaces/tabs).
  - on `204` posts nothing; on `200` with `Content-Type: text/plain` or
    `text/html` (charset ignored, case-insensitive) reads up to 1 MiB and posts
    the body as the bot's message (`canonicalize_body` like the posting API,
    blank → nothing, then `Message::create` + `broadcast_bot_message` with the
    captured base URL, then re-notifies so bot replies can chain to other bots);
    other statuses/content-types log and post nothing. Failures/timeouts log
    and drop (no retries), like other jobs.
- Human `messages#create`/`update` and the bot posting API all call
  `notify_after_message` after broadcast, so creates, edits and bot-to-bot
  mentions all trigger; destroys do not.

  "output": "# Bots

Bots are chat members that post via an HTTP API (`POST /rooms/:room_id/:bot_code/messages`).

## Data model

- `bots` table (Rust-only addition, created via `schema::ADDITIONS` so existing
  Rails databases gain it on boot):
  - `id`, `user_id UNIQUE` (the bot's `users` row, which carries name/avatar and
    memberships), `creator_id` (the human who created it), `bot_code UNIQUE`
    (the credential), `webhook_url NULL` (optional callback), timestamps.
  - Existing databases gain `webhook_url` via `ensure_bots_webhook_column` on boot
    (`ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMN` when missing); fresh databases create it inline.
    Additive only, so Rails keeps working.
- A bot's `users` row has no email and an empty `password_digest` (never used for
  password auth); it is `active`/`member` so existing queries (`User::active`,
  `grant_to_active_users`, room member lists, `autocompletable/users`) treat it like a person.
- Deleting a bot removes its `bots` row, its `users` row's avatar attachment, its
  memberships and sessions/push data is N/A; the `users` row itself is kept when it
  has messages (so history still renders) but marked deactivated? See controller.
  Simpler: keep the user row, delete only the `bots` row + memberships. Posting
  then 401s because the code is gone, while past messages still resolve their
  creator.

Actually implemented: `Bot::destroy` deletes the `bots` row, the bot user's
memberships, its avatar attachment (purge later), and — when the bot has no
messages — its `users` row as well. When messages exist the user row is kept so
`message.creator` still renders (presenter falls back to Unrenderable otherwise,
but keeping the row preserves name/avatar).

## Auth

- UI (`/bots*`) uses the normal session + `require_authentication`.
- `POST /rooms/:room_id/:bot_code/messages` skips session/forgery, authenticates
  by `bot_code` (401 when unknown), 404 when the room is missing. The raw request
  body (`request.raw_post`) is the message body; empty (blank) with no attachment
  is 422. The message is created as `creator = bot.user_id` via `Message::create`
  + `canonical_body`, then `broadcast_create` (same as human `messages#create`),
  which also enqueues the push job via `Room::receive`.

## Webhooks

- The bot form (`/bots/new`, `/bots/:id/edit`) has an optional `Webhook URL`
  field (`bot[webhook_url]`). Blank removes the webhook (`NULL`); the value is
  stored trimmed, with no validation (delivery logs and drops bad URLs).
- Bots are `active` users, so `@`-mention autocomplete (`autocompletable/users`,
  `User.active[.filtered_by].ordered`, optionally scoped to the room's
  memberships) lists them like people. No separate query was needed.
- Whenever a message mentions a bot with a webhook, `bot_webhooks::notify_after_message`
  enqueues an `AdHoc` (`BotWebhook`) job with the room/message ids and the request's
  base URL, then returns: posting never waits for bots. The job:
  - reads the room, message, author, stored HTML (`body_html`), plain text
    (`plain_text_body`) and `mentioned_user_ids` on a reader;
  - looks up `bots_with_webhook_for_user_ids` (webhook `IS NOT NULL`/`!= ''`),
    skipping the author itself so a bot cannot loop on itself;
  - `POST`s each webhook with `Content-Type: application/json` (see `post_json`):
    `Endpoint` from `campfire_richtext::uri::parse` (http/https only, any host —
    no private-network guard so test/local bots work), `Timeouts` 10s open/read
    and a 30s overall deadline, `Connection: close`;
  - payload (relative paths; the bot knows its origin):
    `{ event: "mention", author: {id, name}, room: {id, name, reply_to}, message: {id, body: {text, html}, link} }`
    where `reply_to` is `room_bot_messages(room, bot_code)` (the bot's own
    posting URL), `link` is `room_at_message(room, message)` (deep link),
    `html` is the full stored body, and `text` is the plain text with the bot's
    own `@Name` mention stripped (`stripped_text`: remove all `@BotName`,
    trim, collapse spaces/tabs).
  - on `204` posts nothing; on `200` with `Content-Type: text/plain` or
    `text/html` (charset ignored, case-insensitive) reads up to 1 MiB and posts
    the body as the bot's message (`canonicalize_body` like the posting API,
    blank → nothing, then `Message::create` + `broadcast_bot_message` with the
    captured base URL, then re-notifies so bot replies can chain to other bots);
    other statuses/content-types log and post nothing. Failures/timeouts log
    and drop (no retries), like other jobs.
- Human `messages#create`/`update` and the bot posting API all call
  `notify_after_message` after broadcast, so creates, edits and bot-to-bot
  mentions all trigger; destroys do not.

  with `.switch` + `.switch__btn`; off by default, checked from
  `bot.add_to_all_open_rooms` on edit, preserved on validation errors).
  Parsed with `Account::cast_boolean` (`1` on, `0`/missing off).
- `Bot::create_with_join` / `update_profile_with_join`: when the flag ends up
  on, `join_all_open_rooms` inserts the missing open memberships in the same
  transaction and returns the newly joined `Room`s; turning off only flips the
  flag (memberships kept). Staying on re-joins any missing opens (idempotent).
- New / becoming-open rooms: `Rooms::Opens#create` and `#update` do a second
  write with `Room::grant_auto_join_bots` (flagged bots only) and notify for
  the actually inserted user ids (`RETURNING user_id`, so re-saves notify
  nobody). `grant_to`/`revise`/`insert_memberships` return the inserted ids for
  the same reason.

## `joined`

- `bot_webhooks::notify_after_join(s)` enqueues an `AdHoc` (`BotWebhook`) job
  with `(room_id, bot_id, base_url)`; `deliver_join` re-reads the room+bot,
  skips directs and missing/empty webhooks, then `POST`s:
  `{ event: "joined", room: { id, name, reply_to } }` where `reply_to` is
  `room_bot_messages(room, bot_code)` (relative, like `mention`).
- Direct rooms never notify (`notify_after_join` + `deliver_join` both check
  `room.direct()`).
- Exactly once per membership: controllers only enqueue for `RETURNING`-proven
  inserts (`Bot::join_all_open_rooms` pre-checks, `grant_auto_join_bots` and
  `revise` return inserts, new closed rooms treat every grantee as new).
- Replies work like `mention`: `post_json` → `200 text/plain|text/html`
  (charset ignored, up to 1 MiB, blank → nothing) → `post_bot_reply`
  (`canonicalize_body`, `Message::create`, `broadcast_bot_message` with the
  captured base URL, then `notify_after_message` for chaining). `204`/other
  statuses/content-types and failures log and drop, no retries.
- Manual adds (`Rooms::Closeds#create` for all grantees, `#update`/`revise`
  for `added`) and automatic adds (flag-on create/update, new/becoming-open
  rooms) all go through the same `notify_after_joins`.
